name: Samul nori
lineage: 1978-onward Korean four-instrument concert-percussion ensemble codified by the Kim Duk-soo founding troupe, derived from rural pungmul village-ritual-and-harvest-procession percussion of the late-Joseon era. The four instruments — kkwaenggwari small-gong-leader, jing large-gong-pulse, janggu hourglass-drum, buk barrel-drum — interlock through five canonical jangdan rhythmic-pattern movements (Bibari, Samdo-Sori, Yeongnam, Honam-udo, Jwadodulgi) that compress regional pungmul styles into a 60-90 minute staged concert form. The genre catalyzed the 1980s-onward Korean traditional-music revival and is widely taught in Korean elementary curricula.
